findings: SCOPE/EVIDENCE BASE: all code claims below were verified against the openai/codex repository at HEAD commit d292f721242ef355ce5a38da90e0e33edc4790e6 (2026-10-14), cloned to a local workspace and read as source; repo paths are given as GitHub blob URLs on main (https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/main).

(a) SHIPPED VOICE #1 — Codex inside the ChatGPT desktop app: 'ChatGPT Voice ... lets you talk through ideas and coordinate tasks in Chat, Work, and Codex in the ChatGPT desktop app. Start work, check progress, or change direction without switching back to typing.' Voice is a mode OF A TASK, not a separate agent: 'Open the Codex task you want to discuss ... Select Start voice chat in an existing task, or Start new voice chat in a new chat or task'; 'Voice uses that task's conversation and selected model to carry out your requests, so you can discuss its progress or change direction without starting another task.' Requires a running 'Codex host running the task'; iOS reachable by pairing a phone with a desktop host. Voice dictation is documented as a separate feature from ChatGPT Voice. Sources: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/features/voice ; https://help.openai.com/en/articles/6825453-chatgpt-release-notes ('ChatGPT Voice in Work and Codex on desktop', July 23, 2026 section).

(a) SHIPPED VOICE #2 — GPT-Live-1 is the Voice model: 'ChatGPT Voice is now powered by GPT-Live-1 for paid users and GPT-Live-1 mini for Free users. Both models can listen and speak at the same time ... spoken responses appearing alongside streamed text.' (release notes, July 8, 2026 entry). Codex-side voice is therefore a GPT-Live full-duplex front end over a Codex task, not a Codex model change. Source: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/6825453-chatgpt-release-notes

(a) SHIPPED VOICE #3 — Codex CLI/TUI voice, gated behind an experimental flag: SlashCommand::Voice exists with description 'start or stop voice; use /voice settings to choose a voice' (codex-rs/tui/src/slash_command.rs). The tooltip shipped to users reads: 'NEW: Voice conversations can now be enabled from /experimental. Restart Codex after enabling, then use /voice.' (codex-rs/tui/src/snapshots/codex_tui__tooltips__tests__experimental_voice_tooltip.snap). Runtime gates: 'Voice conversations are not enabled.', 'Voice requires macOS, an MSVC-based Windows build, or a glibc-based Linux build.', 'Voice mode is unavailable in side conversations. Return to the main thread first.' (codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/realtime.rs). URLs: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/tui/src/slash_command.rs , https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/tui/src/tooltips.rs , https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/realtime.rs

(a) SHIPPED VOICE #4 — a separate 'dot' product exists but is NOT a Codex thread author: dots are always-on cloud agents ('your dot has its own cloud computer and browser'), reached by message or a voice call in ChatGPT, and 'can use background agents, start new cloud threads, and create Work or Codex tasks on a connected computer. It can also continue existing local Codex tasks.' i.e. the dot owns the voice conversation and drives Codex through task creation/continuation, not by voice-authoring items inside a Codex thread. Sources: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/dots , https://openai.com/index/introducing-dots/

(b) ARCHITECTURE — voice is a thread-scoped client of app-server, and it does NOT create its own thread: `thread/realtime/start` is keyed by `threadId` (pub thread_id: String, required) and app-server loads that existing thread and subscribes the calling connection before dispatching Op::RealtimeConversationStart (codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/turn_processor.rs, prepare_realtime_conversation_thread + thread_realtime_start_inner). The realtime API surface is: thread/realtime/start, appendAudio, appendText, appendSpeech, stop, listVoices, plus notifications thread/realtime/{started, itemAdded, item/started, item/transcript/delta, item/completed, transcript/delta, transcript/done, outputAudio/delta, sdp, error, closed} — every one of them registered with #[experimental(...)] in codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs (lines ~1080-1118 and ~2044-2065). URLs: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/realtime.rs , https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/common.rs , https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/turn_processor.rs

(b) TRANSPORT — app-server does not proxy the audio for WebRTC: the TUI's own module doc says it is an 'app-server-signaled, locally owned WebRTC voice session' (codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/realtime.rs line 1); server returns the remote SDP via `thread/realtime/sdp` and the client owns the media session. Socket-transport clients instead stream input audio through `thread/realtime/appendAudio` (ThreadRealtimeAudioChunk {data, sampleRate, numChannels, samplesPerChannel, itemId}) and receive `thread/realtime/outputAudio/delta`. Two session identifiers exist: server-side `realtimeSessionId` and a client-generated `voiceSessionId` ('Client-generated identifier for the product voice session'), plus transport ∈ {websocket, webrtc{sdp}, existingCall{callId}} and version ∈ {v1, v2, v3/FramelessBidi}. URLs: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/realtime.rs , https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/realtime.rs

(b) HOW VOICE TEXT REACHES THE CODING THREAD — path 1, 'handoff/delegation': when the realtime model hands work to Codex, core wraps the spoken request as `<realtime_delegation>
  <input>{escaped input}</input>
  <transcript_delta>{tail}</transcript_delta>
</realtime_delegation>` (ContextualUserFragment with content_kind 'realtime_conversation.delegation' and role() == "user") and routes it through Session::route_realtime_text_input, which submits a normal TurnInputRequest::user_input with TurnStartOptions { turn_trigger: Some("realtime") } in StartOrSteer mode (so it starts a turn when idle, or STEERS the active turn otherwise). Sources: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/context/realtime_delegation.rs , https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/session/turn_input.rs , https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/realtime_conversation.rs

(b) HOW VOICE TEXT REACHES THE CODING THREAD — path 2, 'transcript tail flush' at session end (opt-in via flushTranscriptTailOnSessionEnd on thread/realtime/start, default false — 'TODO: Remove this rollout knob once transcript-tail flushing is always enabled'): the remaining transcript is wrapped with an EXTRA in-band marker `<source>transcript_tail_flush</source>` and recorded through the same injection context used by thread/inject_items (session.new_inject_items_context()); record() builds UserInput::Text and emits EventMsg::ItemCompleted { item: TurnItem::UserMessage(UserMessageItem::new(&content)) } into the currently running turn, or fabricates TurnStarted → ItemCompleted → TurnComplete when idle. An app-server integration test asserts exactly this: it lists thread items and finds `ThreadItem::UserMessage { content }` whose text contains '<source>transcript_tail_flush</source>' and 'user: final words'. Sources: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/realtime_conversation/transcript_tail.rs , https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server/tests/suite/v2/realtime_conversation.rs

(b) VOICE ITEMS ARE NOT PART OF STORED THREAD HISTORY: realtime conversation items are persisted to the canonical rollout as RolloutItem::RealtimeItem (protocol RealtimeItem { id, realtime_session_id, content: RealtimeSessionStarted | TranscriptSegment{role: user|assistant, text} | BemItemPromoted | RealtimeSessionClosed }), but the app-server thread-history builder explicitly ignores RealtimeItem — `RolloutItem::... | RolloutItem::RealtimeItem(_) | ... => {}` in build_turns_from_rollout_items — so voice transcript/audio never materializes as a ThreadItem and is not returned by thread/read, thread/resume or thread/fork; it is delivered only as ephemeral thread/realtime/* notifications (README wording at commit 94709228: 'thread/realtime/* notifications are ephemeral transport events, not ThreadItems, and are not returned by thread/read, thread/resume, or thread/fork'). Sources: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/protocol/src/realtime.rs , https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/thread_history.rs , https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/947092283ac3680582fe2fee4b246a61f3c87129

(c) THREAD ITEM MODEL — ThreadItem is a 16-variant tagged union with NO generic role/author field; author identity is implied by the variant: userMessage, hookPrompt, agentMessage, functionCallOutput, plan, reasoning, commandExecution, fileChange, mcpToolCall, dynamicToolCall, collabAgentToolCall, subAgentActivity, imageView, enteredReviewMode, exitedReviewMode, contextCompaction. Source: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs

(c) VOICE-ORIGINATED INPUT IS NOT DISTINGUISHABLE BY ANY STRUCTURED FIELD: the item a voice request produces is `UserMessage { id: String, client_id: Option<String>, content: Vec<UserInput> }` — no source, origin, author, or modality field; UserInput variants are text/image/localImage/audio/localAudio/skill/mention (note: UserInput::Audio exists but is a media-input variant, not an authorship tag; audio input is text-placeholdered out of model requests, TUI rendering and text extraction per commit 97dbd01). The ONLY marker that the message came from voice is IN-BAND, inside the text: the `<realtime_delegation>…<input>…</input></realtime_delegation>` wrapper, and for tail-flush also `<source>transcript_tail_flush</source>`. Sources: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs , https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs , https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/97dbd01a3ddeb47e9162e68066b6e32690d99c5a

(c) HOW OPENAI'S OWN CLI RECOVERS VOICE PROVENANCE — by parsing that in-band wrapper out of userMessage content, i.e. the protocol gives no structured seam: `realtime_delegation_input(items)` string-matches `<realtime_delegation>` / `<input>` on a single UserInput::Text (returning None if there are text_elements), `realtime_delegation_display_text` XML-unescapes it, and the client additionally tracks its own local state: RealtimeTurnOrigin::{Typed{input_generation}, Delegated{may_speak, input_generation}}, latest_input_was_voice, latest_voice_input_fingerprint (hash of the display text), and pending_typed_input matching to decide whether an incoming user message was typed or spoken. A transcript_tail_flush message is detected by literal `.contains("<source>transcript_tail_flush</source>")`. Source: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/realtime.rs

(c) THE STRUCTURED PROVENANCE SEAM THAT DOES EXIST IS TURN-LEVEL, NOT ITEM-LEVEL — and it is public API: `turn/start` accepts `clientUserMessageId` (echoed back as userMessage.clientId), `turnTrigger` ('Optional source classification for the caller that starts this turn'), `parentTurnId` ('Set this when starting work on behalf of another turn, such as delegated work in a different thread. Leave unset for work started directly by the user.') and `rootTurnId`. Core maps these into TurnAttribution { turn_id, turn_trigger, parent_turn_id, initiating_agent_path, root_turn_id }, doc'd as 'Attribution retained across recovery, sleep, and model-context compaction', with TurnInputRequest::on_start documented as 'Options for new turns, also consulted for input provenance'. Value examples found in code/tests: 'realtime', 'user', 'goal', 'queue', 'automation', 'daemon_recovery', 'memory_consolidation', 'page_prompt' — it is a free-form string, not an enum (empty strings are ignored by set_turn_trigger). Sources: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs , https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/protocol/src/turn_input.rs , https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/turn_metadata.rs , https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server/tests/suite/v2/turn_start.rs

(c) BUT THE TRIGGER IS WRITE-ONLY FROM THE CLIENT'S PERSPECTIVE: it is (1) persisted in the rollout, and (2) sent to the MODEL as Responses-API turn metadata under key `turn_trigger` inside `client_metadata["x-codex-turn-metadata"]` (alongside parent_turn_id, root_turn_id, thread_source, subagent_kind, forked_from_thread_id, workspace keys, all in RESERVED_METADATA_KEYS that clients cannot override) — but it is NOT echoed in the read model: the app-server v2 `Turn` is only { id, rootTurnId, items, itemsView, status, error, startedAt, completedAt, durationMs }, and the handler for EventMsg::TurnStarted builds TurnStartedNotification from payload.turn_id / payload.root_turn_id / payload.started_at alone, discarding turn_attribution. So after the fact, neither thread/read, thread/turns/list nor the turn/started notification tells a client that a turn was voice-originated. Sources: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread_data.rs , https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server/src/bespoke_event_handling.rs , https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/responses_metadata.rs

(c) STEERING CANNOT BE ATTRIBUTED: `turnTrigger` and `parentTurnId`/`rootTurnId` are documented as 'Ignored when this request steers an already-active turn' / 'Ignored when this request adds input to an active turn' — so the case that matters most for a live voice plugin (injecting into the in-flight turn) has no structured attribution path at all in the app-server API. Source: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/turn.rs

(c) PRECEDENT THAT CODEX DOES MODEL NON-USER ACTORS — when the actor is NOT the human, Codex adds structured identity at the item level: commandExecution carries `source: agent | userShell | unifiedExecStartup | unifiedExecInteraction`, and secondary agents get their own item types `collabAgentToolCall` (spawnAgent/sendInput/resumeAgent/wait/closeAgent/sendMessage/followupTask/interruptAgent/listAgents) and `subAgentActivity`; hook injections get their own item type `hookPrompt {id, fragments}`. So distinct authorship IS modelled for agents/tools/hooks, but user-shaped input from a non-typing source (voice) has no equivalent. Sources: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs , https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/thread_history.rs

(c) THE CLOSEST THING TO A 'SECONDARY AUTHOR' WRITE PATH IS thread/inject_items: 'Raw Responses API items to append to the thread's model-visible history' (Vec<JsonValue> deserialized into ResponseItem, validated for image URLs, then thread.inject_response_items), explicitly 'without starting a user turn'; those items are persisted to the rollout and reach the model, but the thread-history builder materializes only user-role hook prompts from injected messages, so injected items are invisible in the rendered thread. Sources: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/thread.rs , https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/turn_processor.rs , https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/thread_history.rs

(d) UI SURFACE — desktop app: Voice is a control strip/mode on the Codex task ('Start voice chat' / 'Start new voice chat' / 'Stop voice chat'), with a configurable 'Voice chat hotkey' in Settings > Voice, plan/workspace gating, one active voice chat across the app at a time, spoken responses appearing alongside streamed text, delegation to and from separate tasks ('You can also ask to speak to another Codex task ... Take me back to the previous task'), and macOS Screen-context ('Take a look at this') appshot. There is no documented voice item rendering in the task transcript beyond that, and the docs never describe the protocol used. Sources: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/features/voice , https://help.openai.com/en/articles/6825453-chatgpt-release-notes

(d) UI SURFACE — CLI/TUI: bottom-pane VoiceStrip (voice_strip.rs: 'Renders compact voice controls and caller-owned microphone/speaker sample histories ... show mute only when the current phase permits it. Reduced motion hides the sample-history row') with VoiceStripPhase {Connecting, Active}, microphone_live/microphone_muted, mic+speaker level histories, activity label and mute_hint; footer renders 'voice ● listen · ctrl+m mute' (footer snapshot voice_footer_rendered_styles); voice transcripts are rendered as history cells — user speech via history_cell::new_spoken_user_prompt, voice answers via AgentMarkdownCell::new_spoken — with commands /voice, /voice settings, /voice mute, plus a voice picker and 'Voice conversation started.' / 'Use /voice mute to mute or /voice to stop.' banners. Sources: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/tui/src/bottom_pane/voice_strip.rs , https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/tui/src/history_cell/messages.rs , https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/realtime.rs

(d) UI SURFACE — the one visible authorship affordance in the TUI transcript is a colour, not data: spoken user prompts render with a bold red chevron ('› hello from voice' vs the normal chevron) while the RENDERED RAW TEXT IS IDENTICAL — the test name is literally 'spoken_user_messages_have_a_red_chevron_without_changing_raw_text', and raw_lines() still equals the message. So copy/export/logs cannot tell a spoken prompt from a typed one. Source: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/tui/src/history_cell/messages.rs and its snapshot codex_tui__history_cell__messages__tests__spoken_user_prompt.snap

(d) UI SURFACE — for third-party app-server clients there is no retrieval surface for voice authorship at all: the only voice-related things a client can render are the ephemeral notification streams (transcript/delta and transcript/done carry a bare `role: String`; itemAdded passes a raw JSON item 'while the upstream websocket item schema remains unstable'; outputAudio/delta carries base64 audio + sample rate), which are opt-out-able individually via optOutNotificationMethods. Sources: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/realtime.rs , https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/947092283ac3680582fe2fee4b246a61f3c87129

DOCUMENTATION GAP WORTH NOTING: the published app-server reference at https://developers.openai.com/codex/app-server.md contains ZERO occurrences of 'realtime' or 'voice' — the entire thread/realtime/* surface, its semantics and the ephemerality rule exist only in source, tests and the app-server README revision linked to commit 94709228. Anyone designing against the public docs will not discover that voice is thread-scoped or that voice items are non-ThreadItems.

DIRECT RELEVANCE TO DSH'S DESIGN DECISION: OpenAI's answer is (i) voice attaches to the existing thread rather than owning one, (ii) voice-originated user input lands as a plain userMessage item identical in type to typed input, with provenance only as an in-band XML wrapper plus a UI colour, and (iii) the only first-class, public provenance fields are turn-level (`turnTrigger`, `clientUserMessageId`→clientId, `parentTurnId`, `rootTurnId`), which are model-visible via Responses metadata yet not returned on read and are ignored on steer. A secondary/voice agent can therefore be labelled on turn start, but a voice message injected into a running turn is indistinguishable from typed input in the protocol today; DSH's SessionController.prompt() hard-coding USER provenance matches, rather than diverges from, the leading implementation — the differentiator to steal is the write-side trigger/attribution plus the CLI's spoken-vs-typed visual marker.
shipped_status: MIXED, and the distinction matters. (1) SHIPPED/GA-ish in the desktop product: ChatGPT Voice (GPT-Live-1 full duplex) inside Codex in the ChatGPT desktop app for macOS and Windows, announced July 23, 2026 for Plus/Pro/Business/Edu/Enterprise, with paired-iOS control via a paired desktop host; the ability to start voice in an EXISTING text task is explicitly 'rolling out' and the docs tell users to update 'the desktop app and the Codex host running the task' if the button is missing (and GitHub issue openai/codex#35500 documents the older behaviour where a text-first task could only use dictation). (2) EXPERIMENTAL in Codex CLI/TUI: voice exists but must be enabled via /experimental with a restart, then used as /voice; it is platform-restricted (macOS / MSVC Windows / glibc Linux) and disabled in side conversations, and its own copy calls it 'Voice conversations' rather than a shipped feature. (3) EXPERIMENTAL and undocumented in the app-server protocol: every thread/realtime/* method and notification carries #[experimental(...)] and requires capabilities.experimentalApi; the public app-server reference page mentions neither 'realtime' nor 'voice' at all, so a third party can only learn the surface from source. (4) NOT SHIPPED anywhere in the model: no authorship/provenance field for voice-originated thread items exists in any published or experimental schema; the shipped mechanisms are turn-level trigger/attribution plus in-band text markers plus a UI colour.
ui_surface: Three distinct surfaces, none of which gives voice items their own authored identity in the thread model. (A) Desktop (ChatGPT app, macOS/Windows): voice is a MODE OF THE TASK — 'Start voice chat' in an existing Codex task or 'Start new voice chat' in a new one, 'Stop voice chat' to end, a Settings > Voice hotkey, plan/workspace and permission gating, only one voice chat app-wide at a time, spoken replies streamed alongside text, plus delegation ('it can start separate tasks... brings progress, blockers, and results back to your voice conversation') and task-switching by voice ('Let me talk to the task reviewing the tests'). (B) Codex CLI/TUI: a bottom-pane VoiceStrip widget (Connecting/Active phases, microphone live/muted state, mic+speaker level histories, activity label, mute hint) rendered with a footer status line 'voice ● listen · ctrl+m mute'; voice transcripts appear inline as history cells — user speech as a 'spoken user prompt' with a bold red chevron and voice answers as markdown, with raw text unchanged for copy/export — driven by /voice, /voice settings, /voice mute. (C) App-server clients: no persistent UI data model — only ephemeral notifications (thread/realtime/transcript/delta and transcript/done with a bare role string, itemAdded with raw unstable JSON, outputAudio/delta with base64 audio, sdp, error, closed), individually suppressible via optOutNotificationMethods; voice audio/transcript is deliberately excluded from ThreadItems and from thread/read, thread/resume and thread/fork.
unverified: That the ChatGPT desktop app's Voice-in-Codex (and the paired-iOS path) is implemented on top of app-server's thread/realtime/* API. The docs say only that a 'Codex host running the task' must be updated; the desktop app's source is closed. The API shape (thread-scoped realtime, WebRTC SDP handshake, transcription notifications) and the TUI's use of exactly that API make this the only plausible implementation, but it is inference, not a primary citation.

Whether the desktop app sets turnTrigger (e.g. 'realtime') on turns it originates. Core sets turn_trigger 'realtime' internally for the realtime-routed handoff path (route_realtime_text_input), but no source shows what the desktop/ChatGPT client passes in turn/start.

How the ChatGPT desktop app renders voice-originated items in a Codex task transcript (whether it marks them at all, visually or structurally). No public source describes it; GPT-Live-1 notes only say 'spoken responses appearing alongside streamed text'.

Whether dots' voice calls share any of the Codex realtime plumbing. The dots docs describe calling the dot in the ChatGPT app and the dot creating/continuing Codex tasks, but say nothing about the protocol or about authorship of the resulting turns.

Whether the TUI voice feature is enabled by default in any distribution channel (nightly, specific rollout flag), and the exact config/feature-flag key behind '/experimental' voice; I confirmed the user-facing tooltip, the runtime gate messages and the platform restrictions, not the flag default.

The stability/date provenance of the README wording on realtime notification ephemerality: the current main-branch app-server README no longer documents thread/realtime at all, so that sentence is cited from the revision captured in commit 94709228 rather than from HEAD.
Whether any app-server client today (VS Code extension, other hosts) actually calls thread/realtime/*; only the TUI is confirmed to drive it from in-repo evidence.

Whether openai/codex#35500 (no live Voice in a text-first task) still reproduces in current builds — the official docs now describe 'Voice in existing Codex tasks' as rolling out, so the issue and the docs may both be true for different rollout cohorts.
